# C4 — Inefficient Control Flow

*Level 1 card. 8 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from branching, conditions, or dispatch logic that performs unnecessary checks, uses suboptimal evaluation order, or employs patterns that prevent interpreter optimization. This includes ordering conditions so expensive checks run before cheap ones (poor short-circuit ordering), evaluating conditions that are always true/false (redundant evaluation), using deeply nested branches instead of guard clauses (inefficient nesting), missing mutually-exclusive elif chains (missing else-if), using expensive type introspection in tight loops (expensive comparison), using try/except for frequent exception paths (expensive exception flow), not guarding against trivial edge cases (missing guards), and using non-Pythonic conditional idioms (non-idiomatic condition).

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | Looks for | The repair |
|---|---|---|---|
| **C4.S1** | Poor Short-Circuit Ordering | a boolean chain that evaluates its expensive operand before the cheap one that usually decides | put the cheap, most-decisive test first so short-circuiting can skip the rest |
| **C4.S2** | Redundant Conditional Evaluation | a test whose answer was already settled before it ran | delete the condition whose result is already determined |
| **C4.S3** | Inefficient Conditional Nesting | a nest or chain of branches that tests more than it has to, where a lookup would test once | flatten with guard clauses that return early, or replace a chain of equality arms with a lookup |
| **C4.S4** | Missing Else-If | consecutive `if`s on one subject that are exclusive in fact but not in form | chain the branches with `elif` so evaluation stops at the first match |
| **C4.S5** | Expensive Comparison | a type check made per element where the answer never varies or the types could dispatch themselves | hoist the type decision out of the loop, or dispatch polymorphically |
| **C4.S6** | Expensive Exception Control Flow | an exception used as ordinary control flow, on a path where it is raised often | replace the frequently-raised exception with an explicit check |
| **C4.S7** | Missing Edge-Case Guards | a missing cheap test that would let a common trivial input skip the expensive path | add a cheap guard that skips the expensive path for the trivial case |
| **C4.S8** | Non-Idiomatic Condition | a condition spelled the long way round, missing the interpreter's fast path | use the idiomatic form |

Card paths: `reference/root-causes/C4.S1.md`, `reference/root-causes/C4.S2.md`, `reference/root-causes/C4.S3.md`, `reference/root-causes/C4.S4.md`, `reference/root-causes/C4.S5.md`, `reference/root-causes/C4.S6.md`, `reference/root-causes/C4.S7.md`, `reference/root-causes/C4.S8.md`

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from a category you have already opened is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because something drew you here, which is not the same as a smell being present.
